H1.text: A ladder leaning on a wall. A kite string pulled at a slant. A ramp up to a door.

H2.text: Each is a slanted line, secretly doing two jobs at once.

H3.text: Aarav crosses the college ground in two legs. Twenty metres one way, then fifteen metres another.

H4.text: His friend asks: how far from the start is he now? And in which direction?

H5.text: Drawing it to scale is slow. Components give the answer in seconds.

P2.text: Any vector A has a shadow on the x axis, A x, and a shadow on the y axis, A y.

P3.text: So A equals A x i hat plus A y j hat. One slanted arrow becomes two straight arrows.

S1.text: Now the big idea, live. Aarav's first leg, A, is twenty metres at thirty degrees.

S2.text: Its parts: A x is seventeen point three, A y is ten.

S3.text: His second leg, B, is fifteen metres. Watch what happens as we turn leg B.

S4.text: The x parts stack on the x axis. The y parts stack on the y axis. R joins the start to the finish.

S5.text: Slow motion. Freeze at one hundred and twenty degrees. B x now points left, so it takes away from R x.

S6.text: The graph shows the size of R. It is biggest at thirty degrees, when both legs point the same way.

S7.text: Two legs or ten, the trick is the same. Add the x parts, then add the y parts.

D1.text: Let's write the rule, one step at a time.

D2.text: Step one. Split each vector. A is A x i hat plus A y j hat. B is B x i hat plus B y j hat.

D3.text: Step two. Add them, i hats with i hats, j hats with j hats.

D4.text: Step three. So R x equals A x plus B x, and R y equals A y plus B y.

D5.text: Step four. The size of R is the root of R x squared plus R y squared.

D6.text: And tan theta equals R y over R x. Check the signs to pick the right quadrant.

T1.text: Remember this. Add vectors part by part. x with x, y with y.

C1.text: Subtraction works the same way. Side by side.

C2.text: On the left, A plus B. A is three i plus four j. B is two i minus j. Add the parts. Five i plus three j.

C3.text: On the right, A minus B. Subtract the parts. One i plus five j. Only the signs of B flip.

C4.text: Pause and think. Two vectors add up to give R x equals zero. Must they be equal and opposite? Pause and decide.

C5.text: No! Only their x parts must cancel. Three i plus four j, and minus three i plus two j, add up to six j.

G1.text: Now the signs. They tell you which quadrant R points into.

G2.text: Quadrant one, x and y both positive. Quadrant two, x negative, y positive.

G3.text: Quadrant three, both negative. Quadrant four, x positive, y negative.

G4.text: Now you try. R x is minus four, and R y is plus three. Which quadrant does R point into? Pause and decide.

G5.text: The second quadrant! Negative x is left, positive y is up. Up and to the left is quadrant two.

W2.text: Aarav rides twenty metres at thirty degrees north of east. Then five metres due north. Find his total displacement.

W3.text: First ride. A x is twenty cos thirty, about seventeen point three. A y is twenty sin thirty, which is ten.

W4.text: Second ride. B x is zero. B y is five.

W5.text: Add the parts. R x is seventeen point three. R y is fifteen.

W6.text: Size: the root of seventeen point three squared plus fifteen squared. About twenty two point nine metres.

W7.text: Direction: tan theta is fifteen over seventeen point three. About forty one degrees north of east.

X2.text: Many students find the angle of minus three i plus three j from tan theta equals minus one, and write minus forty five.

X3.text: But that points down and right. Here A x is negative and A y positive, so it is the second quadrant. The angle is one thirty five.

E1.text: Where is this asked? Mostly as a step inside bigger problems, like resolving forces or finding a resultant.

Q1.text: Exam level now. A is six units along plus x. B is six root two units at one thirty five degrees. C is four units along minus y. Find the resultant. Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is A. Two units, along plus y.

A2.text: R x is six, plus six root two times cos one thirty five. That is six minus six. Zero.

A3.text: R y is six root two times sin one thirty five, minus four. That is six minus four. Two.

A4.text: Taking cos one thirty five as positive gives twelve point two. Dropping the minus sign on C gives ten. Both are traps.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. To add two vectors, which parts do you add together?

Y3.text: Two. A is three i plus four j, B is two i minus j. What is A minus B?

Y4.text: Three. Why must you check the signs before finding the angle of R?

N1.text: Next time: velocity and acceleration get x and y parts too, in motion in two dimensions.
